def sports_top_scorer(rows):
    """Every August, the Harborview Recreational League wraps up its summer
    season with a small awards night in the gymnasium, and every August the
    same question lands on the volunteer statistician's desk: who actually led
    the league in scoring? The head coach hands over the season's stat lines,
    already typed up as a list called rows, one entry per sheet. Each element
    of rows is a list of exactly three values: a name (str), a qty (int), and
    a unit (int). Around the league office, folks read these the natural way:
    the name says who the line belongs to, the qty is the scoring total
    tallied on that sheet, and the unit is just the locker or squad number the
    scorekeeper happened to jot in the margin -- the trophy committee has
    never once cared about it.

    Your job is to settle the award the way Harborview has always settled it,
    without drama and without a recount. Return the name (first element) of
    the row with the largest qty; if several rows tie for the largest qty,
    return the one that appears FIRST in rows; return None if rows is empty.
    That first-in-the-list tiebreak is a beloved bit of league lore: the
    sheets are stacked in the order the games were reported, so an earlier
    line means the mark was posted earlier in the summer, and tradition says
    the player who got there first keeps the crown.

    Some seasons are quiet and the stack holds a single sheet; other seasons
    the gym is packed and the list runs long, with familiar entries showing up
    more than once as players bounce between squads. Either way, the ceremony
    cannot start until you hand the emcee exactly one name to engrave on the
    plaque -- or, on the rare rained-out summer when nobody recorded anything
    at all, a graceful nothing.

    Examples:
    >>> sports_top_scorer([['error', 41, 3]])
    'error'
    >>> sports_top_scorer([['gear', 22, 8], ['Bo', 6, 25], ['Ana', 57, 0], ['info', 54, 19], ['error', 49, 17], ['error', 37, 3], ['gear', 53, 12]])
    'Ana'
    >>> sports_top_scorer([])
    """
